newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.4 from 10.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.4 from 10.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate rose 60 basis points to 11.4 percent on Wednesday due to stronger term lending at higher rates, dealers said.
Daily settlements totalled only 37.8 million kuna against 92.8 million on offer.
Some 27.2 million kuna were fresh loans, most of them call money deals at an unchanged rate of 10.5 percent, dealers said.
One six-day interbank loan was granted at 10.5 percent and savings banks took one-month funds at 16, 17 and 18 percent.

Insurers rolled over previous short-term loans at nine percent. Banks prolonged one-week and one-month funds at 10.5 and 15 percent, respectively. But they charged between 16 and 19 percent for the latter to savings banks.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 6.1347 against the dollar and 3.5779 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
